notes: Framing: turned 6° so Jacint Verdaguer runs straight along z. North (the old centre, the Montseny) is at the back; the railway and platform 1 face the camera, so the station's arcade and Nuria's street front are both seen. Was 96° until 2026-10-30, which hid the arcade and put the platform behind the station.

Nuria's street (docs/quests/nuria.md): Carrer de Jacint Verdaguer between Carrer del Doctor Daurella (north) and the Passeig de Pau Gesa (south), one-way, 30 km/h, asphalt with pavements on both sides, cars parked along the east kerb, zebras at both ends.

West side (aerial): Nuria's long two-storey block, white render, two hipped roofs of orange barrel tiles end to end (a valley halfway), a white rim round the eaves, a notch at the south-east corner; small front patios with low walls along the street. North corner: a one-storey house with a flat light-grey metal-sheet roof, a red-tiled terrace and a lawn, hedges and a big tree. Behind: a long grass plot with an old concrete slab, then a taller block of flats on Marià Borrell.

East side (aerial): old terraced houses (cases de cós) with tile roofs and skylights at the Doctor Daurella end, a walled sandy yard, then a walled garden under one huge dark evergreen canopy (about 25 m across) with a hedge along the pavement and a small white shed at the Pau Gesa end. The Museu Arxiu Tomàs Balvey (Casal Daurella, 1848, ground floor and two storeys) stands at Doctor Daurella 1; its garden of Mediterranean medicinal plants opens onto the Passeig de Pau Gesa.

North end: Plaça de Sant Joan (1915) and the town hall, Torre Lligé: a cream villa with a five-arch ground-floor porch under a balustraded terrace, a clock in the central gable, green louvred shutters and a small square belvedere with a hipped roof.

Plaça d'Anselm Clavé: the Fleca Vella de Josep Puig (Can Puig, date stone 1550), three storeys of ochre render with grey granite quoins, a carved Gothic-revival window over an iron balcony, iron letters FLECA VELLA, a granite plinth and a scalloped parapet. Its window sells borregos de Cardedeu, the town's aniseed biscuits (from 1770), most of all in All Saints' week. Forn de pa Domènech is a second bakery nearby.

Santa Maria (16th-18th c.) closes the north edge with Plaça de l'Església in front of its west door; its square bell tower (27 m, Catalan merlons) is the town's skyline, probably the block on the south side towards the Fleca Vella (anchor `campanar`, to confirm). The tiny pre-Romanesque chapel of Sant Corneli stands alone on its gravel square just east.

Station (R2 Nord, R11; the game adds the R4): one storey of butter-yellow render, Arab-tile roof with a scalloped eave course, a taller gabled hall behind an L-shaped porch of four round arches towards platform 1, sandstone-tile bases on the piers, a round clock, iron wall lanterns, a red ticket machine. Platform of grey concrete pavers with a yellow line, about 1 m above the rails; lattice catenary gantries; cone-topped lamps; grey fences; big cedars and a cypress behind; an underpass east of the building. Across Avinguda del Rei En Jaume: cream summer houses with little towers and the salmon-pink Residència Anthurium.

Ground level (EU-DEM 25 m): about 195 m at Doctor Daurella, 194.7 m at Pau Gesa, 193.4 m on Rei En Jaume and at the station, 192.4 m on the tracks, 200 m at the church: a 2 % fall to the south, flat for the game.
Montseny to the north-north-east (Matagalls, Turó de l'Home, Les Agudes, 15-19 km): a broad blue massif with a pale crest, often snow-dusted in winter.
